items.question: Is Cyrrus a digital marketing agency?
items.answer: No. We're a digital transformation consultancy that treats the website and search visibility as what they are for the business: assets that need an owner, a metric, and a return. The practical difference is where the work starts — an agency starts with design or a content calendar; we start by diagnosing which business decision that site needs to enable, and we don't close the project until your team is operating it without us.

items.question: Can I hire just the site, or just the SEO?
items.answer: Yes, and often that's the right call. If the site is already solid and fast, there's no reason to rebuild it — only visibility work is needed. If the site is slow or doesn't convert, investing in positioning before fixing it just sends more visitors to a door that won't open. The initial diagnosis defines which of the two fronts pays off first.

items.question: How does Digital Presence connect to the CIRA method?
items.answer: It runs on the same four phases: we diagnose what the business needs (Construct), evaluate platforms and tools without commercial bias (Identify), execute with project governance (Realize), and train your team to sustain it (Adopt). It isn't a separate service with a different logic.

items.question: Is it worth talking to Cyrrus if we already work with an agency?
items.answer: Yes. In several cases the diagnosis concludes that the agency is doing its part well and the problem sits earlier: there's no clarity on what the site needs to achieve, or no one on the client side is measuring the result. We can build on what already exists instead of proposing you start from zero.

items.question: What is corporate web development?
items.answer: It's building a company's website as a business asset, not as a communications piece. It differs from a template-built site in three ways: it starts from a content architecture that answers the buyer's real questions, it's built with measurable performance and accessibility requirements, and it's delivered with analytics configured and the client's team trained to run it. For an executive, the value is that the site stops being an image expense and starts showing up as a source of leads with a known cost and return.

items.question: How long does corporate web development take?
items.answer: It depends on scope, but the typical range for a corporate site with its own content architecture runs six to twelve weeks from the close of the diagnosis. What extends a project most isn't development — it's defining the content on the client's side. That's why we start content architecture in week one, in parallel with design, instead of waiting for all the copy to be ready before starting.

items.question: Does an existing corporate site need to be rebuilt from scratch?
items.answer: Not necessarily, and the diagnosis exists precisely to answer that before quoting anything. In plenty of cases the current site has a reasonable foundation and the real problem is performance, content structure, or lack of measurement — three things fixed on top of what exists, at a fraction of the cost of rebuilding. Rebuilding is justified when the platform prevents measuring, growing, or publishing without an outside provider.

items.question: Who can update the site after delivery?
items.answer: Your team. Delivery includes a content manager and the training to use it, because the most common reason a corporate site goes stale isn't a lack of content — it's the friction of having to request every change from a provider. If you'd also rather leave ongoing maintenance to us, that's arranged separately — but never as a forced dependency.

items.question: Does development include search engine positioning?
items.answer: The site is delivered with the technical foundation positioning needs: semantic structure, speed, structured data, and content organized by search intent. The ongoing positioning work — keyword research, content, authority, and visibility in AI answer engines — is the SEO service, which can be hired alongside the site or afterward.

items.question: What is SEO and why does a B2B company need it?
items.answer: SEO is the work of making a company appear in search results when someone searches for the problem that company solves, without paying for every click. It matters more in B2B than in other sectors for a concrete reason: the buyer of an enterprise solution researches for weeks before contacting anyone, and makes that decision by reading, not by watching ads. If your company isn't present during that research stage, it enters the conversation once the provider is practically already chosen.

items.question: What is GEO and how is it different from SEO?
items.answer: GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is optimization for AI answer engines — ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, and Google's generated answers. The practical difference from traditional SEO is the outcome pursued: SEO competes for a position in a list of links; GEO competes to be the source the model cites within its answer. The techniques shift — the structure of the information, the density of verifiable data, and AI crawler access matter far more — but the two are worked together, because they share the same technical and content foundation.

items.question: How long does SEO take to show results?
items.answer: Technical fixes can move rankings within weeks, because they correct something that was actively blocking the search engine. Positioning through content and authority is measured in months: three to six to see sustained movement in competitive searches. Anyone promising top rankings in thirty days is either buying links or targeting searches no one makes. What is reported from month one is implementation progress and the change in technical metrics.

items.question: Does SEO replace paid ad spend?
items.answer: It doesn't replace it, it makes it optional. Paid ads and SEO solve different moments: ads buy immediate visibility and stop existing when the budget turns off; SEO builds an asset that keeps bringing demand. Most companies that work positioning well don't stop running ads — they stop depending on them, which is a very different financial situation.

items.question: Can we start SEO right away on a newly launched site?
items.answer: Yes, and it's the best time. When structure, speed, and structured data are defined during the site's construction, positioning work starts on a healthy foundation instead of spending the first months fixing decisions already made.
